questions.question: fns = [lambda: i for i in range(3)]; print([f() for f in fns]) — output?
questions.answer: [2, 2, 2] — closures variable ko late bind karte hain, isliye sab last value dekhte hain. Fix: default argument se bind karo: [lambda i=i: i for i in range(3)].
questions.explanation: Late binding closure trap.

questions.question: def f(x, acc=[]): acc.append(x); return acc → f(1) phir f(2) ka output?
questions.answer: f(1) → [1], f(2) → [1, 2]. Default list definition time par ek hi object hai, isliye calls ke beech share hoti hai (same mutable-default trap, function version).

questions.question: Ye function UnboundLocalError deta hai: def f(): print(x); x = 1 → wajah?
questions.answer: Assignment hone se x poore function me local maana jaata hai, isliye print se pehle x unbound hai. print global value dikhani ho to global declare karo ya function param banao — global mutation se better param hai.
questions.explanation: Assignment = local scope.

questions.question: Decorator lagane ke baad function ka naam __main__.wrapper ho gaya aur docstring gayab. Fix?
questions.answer: functools.wraps(fn) laga do wrapper par — isse __name__, __doc__ aur metadata copy ho jaate hain (original function wrapper.__wrapped__ me milta hai).
questions.explanation: wraps metadata bachata hai.

questions.question: Function galat values return kar raha hai kyunki ek branch me return missing hai. Robust fix kaise karoge?
questions.answer: Har branch me explicit return likho aur default path par error raise karo (ya typing se None return annotate karo). Test me woh branch specifically cover karo — silent None control-flow bug ka sabse aam source hai.
questions.explanation: Explicit return + branch test.

questions.question: Code me list = [...] likha aur baad me list(...) call kar raha hai — kya galat aur fix?
questions.answer: Builtin list ko shadow kar diya, isliye builtin constructor unavailable ho gaya. Fix: variable ka naam badlo (items), aur lint (flake8 A001/B006 family) use karo taaki shadowing pakdi jaaye.
questions.explanation: Builtin shadowing mat karo.

questions.question: Real-world: flaky network call ke liye retry decorator likho (bounded attempts + backoff).

questions.question: Real-world: partial application se ek general function ko fixed-config version me convert karo.

def fetch(url, timeout=5, retries=2):

print(fetch_fast('https://x'))

questions.question: Project defense: 'Tumhare project me decorators kahan use kiye aur kya fayda mila?'

questions.question: Project defense: 'Tumne typing hints use kiye ya nahi — kyun?'

questions.question: Project defense: 'Ek 200-line function ko tumne kaise refactor kiya?'

questions.question: Compare: **kwargs ko basic level par explain karo aur ek AI/data use case batao.

questions.question: `def f(x, acc=[]): acc.append(x); return acc` ko do baar call karo — `f(1)` phir `f(2)` — second call ka return value kya hoga?
questions.answer: `[1, 2]` — default argument ek hi list object function definition par banti hai aur har call me reuse hoti hai. Isliye pehli call ka effect doosri call me dikhta hai; `None` sentinel + `bucket = [] if bucket is None else bucket` se fix hota hai.
questions.explanation: Pehle output predict karo, phir compare karo.

questions.question: `def add(a, b=10): return a + b` par `add(5)` aur `add(5, 1)` — dono calls me `a`, `b` aur return value likho.
questions.answer: `add(5)` → a = 5, b = 10 (default laga), return 15. `add(5, 1)` → a = 5, b = 1 (default override hua), return 6. Keyword form `add(a=5, b=1)` bhi same deta hai — positional pehle bind hota hai, default tab lagta hai jab argument missing ho.
questions.explanation: Pehle output predict karo, phir compare karo.

questions.question: Function expected value ki jagah `None` return kar raha hai — pehla suspect kya hai?
questions.answer: Koi code path `return` ke bina khatam ho raha hai (silent fall-through) — Python har function se implicitly `None` return karta hai. Har branch ka return check karo, aur `-> int` type hint + mypy se ye statically pakdo.

questions.question: Kaun sa edge case is function ko todta hai: `def avg(nums): return sum(nums) / len(nums)`?
questions.answer: Khaali list — `sum([])` 0 deta hai par `len([])` 0 hai, isliye `ZeroDivisionError`. Guard lagao: `if not nums: return None` (ya 0.0), aur contract document karo taaki caller `None` handle kare. Ek aur edge: `None` values wali list (`TypeError`).
questions.explanation: Pehle output predict karo, phir compare karo.

questions.question: Validation function ke andar ho ya caller par?
questions.answer: System boundary par validate karo (input function me aate hi, ek hi jagah), phir andar ke reusable helpers bharosa karein. Isse har internal call ke liye duplicate checks nahi likhne padte, aur error message bhi boundary par hi achha likha ja sakta hai.

questions.question: Reusable function likhne me pehle kya optimize karoge: kam lines, readability, ya testability?
questions.answer: Readability + testability pehle — single-purpose chhota function likho jo alag se test ho sake; premature generalisation (har jagah `**kwargs`, flexible flags) se bacho. Performance sirf measurement ke baad tune karo, kyunki read karna hi sabse zyada karna padta hai.
